Simulate an example dataset for the propensity model sensitivity diagnostics

Source: R/simulate_example_data.R
simulate_example_data.Rd

Generates one dataset from the data-generating mechanisms of the simulation study. Six standard normal covariates x1 to x6; in Scenario 5 four binary covariates b1 to b4 are added, b4 rare at 5 %. The true treatment logit is alpha + X beta + nonlinear(X), where alpha is solved numerically so that the mean true propensity over the generated patients equals treated_share. The outcome is y = mu0 + tau * treat + noise with mu0 = X gamma + lambda * nonlinear(X).

Usage

simulate_example_data(
  n,
  scenario = c("S1", "S2", "S3", "S4", "S5"),
  lambda = 0,
  treated_share = 0.2,
  seed = 1,
  heterogeneity = FALSE
)

Arguments

n

Number of patients (positive integer).

scenario

One of "S1", "S2", "S3", "S4", "S5".

lambda

Strength of the nonlinear terms in the outcome model: 0 means the nonlinear terms affect treatment but not the outcome (harmless misspecification); the plan uses 1.5 for the harmful case.

treated_share

Target mean true propensity, in (0, 1). Default 0.20.

seed

Integer seed.

heterogeneity

If TRUE, the treatment effect is tau = 1 + 0.8 * x1; otherwise tau = 1 for everyone.

Value

A data frame with one row per patient and columns id, x1 to x6, (b1 to b4 for Scenario 5), treat (0/1), y, mu0, tau, true_logit, true_propensity. Attributes scenario, lambda, treated_share, seed, heterogeneity and alpha record the settings.

Details

Draw order: the covariates, the treatment and the outcome noise are drawn first and do not depend on lambda or heterogeneity, so for a given scenario and seed they are identical for every lambda; lambda enters only mu0 and y.

Scenarios:

  • "S1" correct model: no nonlinear term.

  • "S2" squared terms: 0.7 (x1^2 - 1) + 0.7 (x2^2 - 1).

  • "S3" interactions: 0.9 x1 x2 + 0.9 x2 x3.

  • "S4" poor overlap: no nonlinear term, beta scaled by 2.5.

  • "S5" mixed: S2 and S3 terms plus the four binary covariates (fixed coefficients).

The function sets the random seed with set.seed(seed) and restores the previous state of the random number generator on exit.

Examples

example_data <- simulate_example_data(n = 500, scenario = "S2", lambda = 1.5, seed = 1)
head(example_data)
